A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F-Fidelity work. The main text and Appendices A–E, including embedded plots, support reliable matching of methods, theory and experiments despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original explainer-ranking experiments across images, time series and NLP, together with colored-MNIST explanation-size experiments, ablations and sensitivity studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds backbone comparisons, robustness and explanation-preservation analyses, ImageNet evaluations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: V2 corrects the reported non-explanation removal cap from βtd/s to βtd/(td−s), and Algorithm 1 restores the missing td factors in its caps. These are local procedural corrections; the fine-tuning loss and overall fine-tuning-plus-stochastic-removal framework remain.

E1.justification: Appendix D.10 adds evaluation on an ImageNet subset at 224×224 resolution. The existing CIFAR-100, Tiny-Imagenet, PAM, Boiler, SST2, BoolQ and colored-MNIST coverage remains. NLP and explanation-size experiments are relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: The competing evaluation methods remain Fidelity, ROAR and R-Fidelity, with Fidelity+Fine-tune retained in the ablation. LayerCAM and Saliency Map expand the explainers being assessed; GinX-Eval is cited but not evaluated against F-Fidelity.

E3.justification: New protocols include CNN time-series backbones, LayerCAM explanations, prediction-agreement measurements and ImageNet fine-tuning on 5,000 images with evaluation on 500 images from that same set. V2 also specifies four BoolQ Transformer layers where v1 specified eight; this reported setting revision does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct tests of perturbation robustness, decision and attribution preservation after fine-tuning, an individual degraded-explanation case study, comparisons of undegraded explainers and computational efficiency analyses (Appendices D.2–D.6 and D.10–D.11). V1's component ablation, explanation-size experiments and hyperparameter studies are retained.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting and error-bar practices remain. The default number of stochastic mask samples stays at 50, with T renamed N. Neither version supplies a repeated-run/seed protocol, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical entries, while v2 adds CNN, LayerCAM, robustness, explainer-comparison and timing results; Table 13 reports 4,026 seconds for F-Fidelity versus 7,378 for ROAR. BoolQ Transformer micro MoRF–LeRF correlations change from +1.00 in v1 Table 9 to −1.00 in v2 Table 7. Several original backbone-accuracy entries disappear.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the formal non-explanation sampling count and bound to use td−s, and replaces the undefined probability expression in the Shapley marginal with conditional label probabilities. Theorem 1, its influence-tier assumptions and the substantive proof in Appendix B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: explanation-agnostic fine-tuning and controlled removal improve faithfulness evaluation across modalities, and explanation size can be recovered under the stated faithful-explainer conditions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of preserving model behavior, the tradeoff between masking robustness and agreement with the original model, and explanation preservation. Section 5.4 gives explicit guidance on choosing evaluation metrics based on model robustness. Appendix D.10 restricts applicability of the ImageNet model fine-tuned on the evaluation pool.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code link, explicit NLP LSTM and training-epoch details, and sample/budget information for new comparisons. It drops the NLP token-embedding dimensions stated in v1. Existing defaults of β=0.1 and 50 mask samples are consolidated in Appendix C rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: V2 adds GinX-Eval to related work and references for noise regularization, dropout, LSTM and Saliency Map. It expands the explanation of ROAR's information leakage and computational cost. The R-Fidelity reference changes from preprint to conference publication, representing the same work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: theory precedes experiments, NLP moves into the main text, and explanation-size verification moves into the appendix. Background and method explanations are extensively revised, and Appendix D is reorganized around the expanded analyses.

P2.justification: V2 adds decision-agreement and case-study figures plus robustness, attribution, explainer-comparison and timing tables. It regroups NLP tables by architecture, consolidates explanation-size plots, removes standalone accuracy summaries and fixes the clipped BoolQ plot table from v1 Table 19 in v2 Table 23.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects operational masking formulas and directly examines a central validity concern largely untested in v1: whether fine-tuning changes the model and explanations being evaluated. The preservation studies, explicit robustness tradeoffs, practical guidance and measured computational costs substantially strengthen justification and usability. Overlapping ImageNet tuning/evaluation data, reduced accuracy disclosures and the unexplained BoolQ configuration revision remain limitations, but do not outweigh these gains.
